findings.claim: Across the full observed score window [0.0,0.49], the landmark_00 local displacement components show non-monotone, sign-changing trajectories rather than a stationary target: landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts, landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with 4 strong sign conflicts, and landmark_00_local_dz has 10 sign changes with 7 strong sign conflicts.

The landmark_00 displacement curves are not well described by a low-degree polynomial over the observed support: polynomial_accepted is false for landmark_00_local_dx (degree 2, relative_node_RMSE 0.78), landmark_00_local_dy (degree 1, relative_node_RMSE 0.67) and landmark_00_local_dz (degree 3, relative_node_RMSE 0.72), so no single smooth trend is supported across the whole window.

landmark_00_soft_mass is the most coherent of the read features: it has only 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict, polynomial_accepted is false but relative_node_RMSE is 0.29, and its whole-window z is positive (0.64) with a positive early rise and a late decline.

landmark_10 displacement components are similarly non-monotone: landmark_10_local_dx has 6 sign changes with 13 strong sign conflicts, landmark_10_local_dy has 7 sign changes with 3 strong sign conflicts, and landmark_10_local_dz has 6 sign changes with 8 strong sign conflicts; none has polynomial_accepted true.

landmark_10_soft_mass shows a positive whole-window z (0.40) with 4 sign changes and 2 strong sign conflicts, and its early rate z is strongly positive (66.3) while its late rate z is negative (-11.6), indicating a rise-then-fall shape within the observed window.

The observed score clock covers 50 nodes from 0.0 to 0.49 with learning_window [0.0,0.5]; all curve supports are restricted to [0.0,0.49] and extrapolation_allowed is false for every read feature, so no evidence exists beyond the observed support.

hypotheses.direction: test a non-constant temporal dose against the constant-dose reference, without asserting which phase is optimal
hypotheses.falsifier: If the non-constant schedule produces the same realized total delivered displacement and the same endpoint affinity as the constant-dose reference, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: whole-window shape of landmark soft-mass and local displacement z-profiles over observed score nodes 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00 and landmark_10 soft-mass coordinates rise through the early-to-middle portion of the observed window and then decline toward its end, while the displacement components oscillate with multiple sign changes; a temporal dose schedule that is not constant across the window is therefore worth testing against a constant-dose reference, with the expectation that any timing benefit must be separated from a change in total delivered displacement.

limitations: Only landmark_00 and landmark_10 features were read; the remaining 180 catalogue curve features are unqueried, so no claim is made about them.
No stage profiles or temporal profiles are available; all statements rest on the continuous curve handles.
Selection preference and curve shape are associations, not measured final affinity benefit; decoded final quality is not observed in this role input.
All curves are restricted to the observed support [0.0,0.49] with extrapolation disallowed; nothing is claimed for the remaining native horizon.
The read curves are coordinate proxies without a typed energy or chemical-interaction interpretation.
